title: Linear API Integration Guide: GraphQL, Webhooks, Auth (2026)
summary: The Linear API uses GraphQL queries to manage project workflows and sync data. Developers can authenticate via OAuth2 to build custom tool connections.
body_markdown:
## Scaling Linear workflows without custom infrastructure


Building on an abstraction layer removes the need to maintain a persistent server just to catch a webhook or map a JSON payload to a GraphQL mutation.


> **A robust automation platform provides this production-ready environment for teams who need to bypass the overhead of managing OAuth tokens and webhook listeners manually. If a specific connector is missing from the 750 integrations in the open-source monorepo, you can generate it with AI and add it privately to your instance without waiting for a vendor release. Roughly 60% of integrations are community-contributed, meaning the catalogue expands based on actual user needs rather than a closed vendor roadmap.**


### Using the Linear connector for zero-code mutations


The Linear connector eliminates the need to construct complex GraphQL mutations by providing a visual interface for issue and project management. Instead of manually defining input objects for the issueCreate mutation, you map data directly into fields for titles, descriptions, and team assignments.


### Automating issue syncs across Jira or GitHub


Bridging Linear with other project management tools requires a translator that understands different ID formats and state machines.


Jira (a project tracking tool for enterprise teams) uses a different status hierarchy than Linear, requiring a logic step to map "In Progress" to "Started."


GitHub (a developer platform for version control) triggers workflows based on pull request events that must be linked to specific Linear issue keys.


Slack (a team communication platform) is the destination for real-time alerts when high-priority issues are blocked.


The following canvas demonstrates a typical notification workflow where a Stripe payment failure triggers an immediate alert in a Slack channel.


574ms is all it took for the data to reach its destination without custom retry logic, as shown in this visual confirmation. Once these notifications are active, you can scale to more complex synchronization tasks.


Modern workflow engines handle these promotions through Git Sync and Release Management, moving flows from test environments to production as versioned software rather than private in-app saves.


This deliberate promotion step is why MoneyGram and FundingSocieties run the platform in production to manage their automation environments. You can verify these capabilities in the technical documentation for Release Management, which applies the same logic to both self-hosted and cloud instances.


### Centralizing webhook management for incoming signals


Centralizing webhook management replaces the brittle process of hardcoding secret keys into environment variables across multiple microservices. The dashboard is a single location to monitor the health of incoming signals from Linear, allowing you to rotate signing secrets or update endpoint URLs without redeploying code.
